 The Oregon Ducks' resurgence began with a pivotal team meeting after the Illinois loss. Chris Wuensch | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Nov. 7, 2026; Columbus, Ohio; Oregon coach Dan Lanning yells after calling a timeout against the Ohio State Buckeyes at Ohio Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Oregon Ducks Michigan State Spartans No. 13 Oregon (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten) had just lost for the second time in three games, falling 21-10 to Illinois to drop to 4-3 on the year.
--> No. 13 Oregon (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten) had just lost for the second time in three games, falling 21-10 to Illinois to drop to 4-3 on the year.
 With the Ducks’ back against the wall, coach Dan Lanning called a team meeting to refocus his squad’s mindset. From there, Oregon has been a rejuvenated team , reeling off wins over Northwestern, Ohio State and Michigan to restore its postseason hopes.

Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon outside linebacker Nasir Wyatt revealed the meeting’s significance to reporters on Wednesday at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex.
--> Oregon outside linebacker Nasir Wyatt revealed the meeting’s significance to reporters on Wednesday at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex.
 Wyatt is among those stepping up in the absence of star outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti , who was injured versus the No. 14 Buckeyes (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten). The sophomore rang up a pair of tackles for loss, including a sack to bring his season total up to 3.5 sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss.

 Wyatt shared his respect for Rushing, discussed the season-saving team meeting and tuning out any outside noise ahead of Friday’s showdown with Michigan State.
--> Wyatt shared his respect for Rushing, discussed the season-saving team meeting and tuning out any outside noise ahead of Friday’s showdown with Michigan State.
 Dan Lanning’s Message Sparks Change
--> Dan Lanning’s Message Sparks Change
 Oct. 31, 2026; Eugene, Oregon; Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning yells to his team against the Northwestern Wildcats at Autzen Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect “Really, after the Illinois game, that team meeting Coach Lanning had with us was a moment to shift. He was telling us we’ve got to go back to our traits, the things that got us here. Playing fast, just letting it hang, like he says all the time. Just being you, doing your job. And I feel like once the whole team felt how Coach Lanning was acting, we all just hopped on board.”

 Playing for Injured Teitum Tuioti
--> Playing for Injured Teitum Tuioti

Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “It was definitely hard. I mean, T, he meant so much to us and the team as for his leadership and just the way he carries himself every day. He’s a fighter, and I have the utmost respect for him. I want to take all the opportunities I had and just do it for him, because I just know how bad he wants this too. I just know how bad he wants to still be out there.”

He’s still being vocal. He’s still talking. He’s never going to lose his leadership because that’s just the way he is. He’s a real humble guy, and that’s why I respect him. He definitely knows what’s on the line, and he’s going to get it. He works so hard for it. He’s been working for four years now.
